# tapectl setup

[All commands](README.md)

Set up tapectl for one drive on your own account, step by step

For one person with one tape drive on their own Linux account (a host with a service user is set up by scripts/first-run.sh instead). Each step says what it is about to do, then what it did: the home (~/.tapectl unless --home names another); a staging directory; the drive, found under /dev/tape/by-id/ with its generation read from its model (the tape is never opened); the operator's keys and a new escrow identity, whose secret is printed once on stderr, as `init` prints it (under --yes too), to copy onto paper, and stored nowhere; two locations; a first collection, its units registered on yes; weekly catalog-backup and audit timers as systemd user units (files only); `config check`. Then what needs root, as one block for you to run (setup never runs sudo), and the commands for the first two copies.

A step already done is skipped, so a run that stopped is finished by running setup again, and a run on a finished home changes nothing. Each question has its flag; --yes takes every default and refuses a question that has none, naming its flag; --dry-run says what each step would do and changes nothing. Without a terminal, setup needs --yes or --dry-run.

```text
tapectl setup [OPTIONS]
```

**Options**

- `--staging <DIR>` — Directory for staged slices: ideally a big disk that is not the source
  
    Created when it does not exist (setup asks first). Default: the staging directory config.toml already names, `<home>/staging` in a new home.
- `--device <PATH>` — The tape drive's node, preferably its /dev/tape/by-id/…-nst link
  
    Default: the one drive under /dev/tape/by-id/; with several, setup asks which. A /dev/nstN is written as the by-id link that names it, when one does. Only the drive's identity is read (from the kernel's records); the tape is never opened.
- `--generation <GEN>` — The generation the drive writes, e.g. LTO-6 (default: its model's)
  
    As for `drive add`: needed when the drive is not attached now or its model is not one tapectl knows.
- `--operator <NAME>` — The operator's name (default: this account's login name)
- `--escrow-public-key <KEY_OR_FILE>` — Adopt this escrow public key instead of minting a new escrow identity
  
    An age1… literal, or a path to a .pub file, as for `init --escrow-public-key`. Left out, setup mints one as `init` does: its secret is printed once on stderr (under --yes too, terminal or not), to copy onto paper, and stored nowhere (ADR-0005).
- `--location <NAME>` — A place cartridges are kept; give it twice (default: home, offsite)
- `--collection-root <DIR>` — The folder whose subfolders are the units, e.g. /media/photos
  
    The first collection's root. It has no default: under --yes, setup refuses without it.
- `--collection <NAME>` — The first collection's name (default: its folder's name)
- `--tenant <NAME>` — The tenant the collection's units belong to (default: the operator)
  
    Added when it does not exist.
- `--backup-dir <DIR>` — Directory for the weekly catalog backup, best on another disk
  
    Default: ~/tapectl-backups (setup warns when it is on the home's disk).
- `--no-timers` — Write no systemd user timers for the backup and the audit
